hero.label: Graz → Prague
hero.intro: Graz to Prague by private chauffeur is a 450 km door-to-door transfer north through Styria and Upper Austria via Linz, then across South Bohemia, around 4.5 to 5 hours drive time. Prestigo’s fixed fare starts at €{ePrice} in a Mercedes-Benz E-Class, tolls and both Austrian and Czech vignettes included. Pickup from any Graz address or Graz Airport (GRZ), drop-off anywhere in Prague.
hero.imageAlt: Private chauffeur transfer from Graz to Prague in a Mercedes

openingParagraphs: A private transfer from Graz to Prague covers 450 km — north on the A9 Pyhrn motorway through Styria and Upper Austria to Linz, the S10 to the Czech border at Wullowitz–Dolní Dvořiště, then České Budějovice and the D3 motorway via Tábor to Prague — and takes approximately 4.5 to 5 hours door to door. The fixed fare starts at €{ePrice} in a Mercedes E-Class for up to 3 passengers; groups of up to 6 travel in the V-Class from €{vPrice}; the S-Class is available from €{sPrice} for executive or VIP travel. Your chauffeur collects you from your hotel in the Old Town, an office, Graz Hauptbahnhof or Graz Airport, and drops you at the door of your Prague address.

The fare is set when you book and stays that way: fuel, tolls, the Austrian and Czech vignettes, bottled water, Wi-Fi and child seats on request are included. No change of trains in Vienna, no luggage carried between platforms, no taxi to find in Prague.

routeNarrative.headingItalic: in four and a half to five hours.
paragraphs: From a pickup below the Schlossberg, in the university quarter or at Graz Airport south of the city, your chauffeur takes the A9 Pyhrn motorway north through the Styrian valleys and the tunnels under the Gleinalpe and the Bosruck into Upper Austria. The tunnel sections carry their own tolls, already in your fare. The motorway comes down the Krems valley and joins the A1 for the short run to Linz on the Danube, where the route turns north on the S10 Mühlviertel expressway.

The Austrian–Czech border at Wullowitz–Dolní Dvořiště is a Schengen crossing — no stop, no document check in normal conditions. On the Czech side the road runs past Kaplice to České Budějovice, and the D3 motorway carries you north through Tábor to Prague. Total distance is approximately 450 kilometres; driving time is four and a half to five hours in normal traffic.

Your chauffeur checks the Pyhrn tunnels, the S10 and the D3 before you leave and adjusts the route around roadworks without asking. If you want an afternoon in Vienna on the way, that is possible as an optional detour — tell us at booking. Either way, you arrive in Prague with the evening still ahead of you.

includedIntro: The fixed price covers everything between your Graz pickup and your Prague drop-off: the car, the chauffeur, fuel, the Austrian and Czech vignettes and every toll. Whether you are travelling for business, a city break or the next leg of a longer tour, you step out in Prague with nothing to arrange.

Upper Austria’s capital on the Danube, where the Pyhrn motorway ends and the route turns north — a natural place for a coffee or a short walk along the river.
The South Bohemian capital, where the road joins the D3 for the last stretch to Prague. A good place to break the drive.
A castle in Český Krumlov, a viewpoint, a restaurant you want to try? Tell us at booking. The route is yours.

goodToKnow.label: Border crossing
goodToKnow.value: Austrian–Czech Schengen border at Wullowitz–Dolní Dvořiště. No routine passport check — non-EU passengers should still carry their passport and visa.

goodToKnow.label: Tolls
goodToKnow.value: Austrian and Czech motorway vignettes and all tolls on the route, including the Pyhrn tunnel sections, are included in the quoted price.

goodToKnow.label: Airport pickup
goodToKnow.value: Give us your flight number. Your chauffeur tracks the landing at Graz Airport and adjusts the pickup time automatically. 60 minutes of waiting is free.

goodToKnow.label: Return transfer
goodToKnow.value: Heading back to Graz later? Book both directions together for the same day and the return leg is 10% off.

dayTrip.intro: A drive of this length is easier with a break, and the road from Graz to Prague passes three places worth an hour of your time.

configurations.title: Linz on the Danube
configurations.body: Leave Graz at 8:30 and reach Linz a little before 11:00. Walk the Hauptplatz, look in at the Ars Electronica Center or take coffee by the river, then north across the border to Prague by late afternoon.
configurations.price: Add a stop at booking — contact us for a quote.

configurations.title: Lunch in Český Krumlov
configurations.body: A short detour after the border brings you to Český Krumlov, a UNESCO town wrapped in a bend of the Vltava. Ninety minutes for the castle courtyards and lunch by the river, then two and a half hours on to Prague.
configurations.price: Add a stop at booking — contact us for a quote.

configurations.title: České Budějovice and Hluboká
configurations.body: Stop at the arcaded main square of České Budějovice, home of the Budweiser Budvar brewery, or at the white château of Hluboká a few minutes north. One hour is enough, and from there it is about two hours on the D3 to Prague.
configurations.price: Add a stop at booking — contact us for a quote.

dayTrip.footnote: Stops are planned at booking and priced by the extra time and distance — tell us where you would like to stop and we confirm a firm quote before you book. A short coffee or rest stop on the motorway is always included.

chauffeurNarrative: Your chauffeur pulls up at the door of your Graz hotel, ready at the agreed time. At Graz Airport they wait inside the Arrivals hall with a name board, watch your flight, and see your luggage into the car.

Four and a half to five hours is a long stretch, and it is yours to use. Prepare for tomorrow, make calls, or sleep — your chauffeur keeps conversation to whatever you want. If you are new to Prague, ask about the city: where your hotel is, which streets are pedestrian-only, how to spend a first evening.

Water, a charger and Wi-Fi are already in the cabin. A break at a motorway rest stop is planned along the way, and you choose when. When you reach Prague, your chauffeur takes the bags to reception and you walk straight in.

items.title: A fixed fare for the full distance
items.body: Fuel, tolls, the Austrian and Czech vignettes and driver time are all in the price you book. A long route does not mean extras at the end.

items.title: No change in Vienna
items.body: There is no quick direct rail link from Graz to Prague. By car your luggage is loaded once in Graz and comes out at your Prague door, with no platform in between.

items.title: A Prague company
items.body: Prestigo is based in Prague and runs its own Mercedes fleet. Your chauffeur knows the city you are arriving in — the hotel entrances, the one-way streets and the quickest way to your address.

faqs.q: How long does a private transfer from Graz to Prague take?
faqs.a: Approximately 4.5 to 5 hours door to door: the A9 Pyhrn motorway north to Linz, the S10 to the Wullowitz–Dolní Dvořiště border, then České Budějovice and the D3 to Prague. Friday afternoon traffic into Prague or roadworks in the Pyhrn tunnels can add 20–30 minutes.

faqs.q: How much is a taxi or chauffeur from Graz to Prague?
faqs.a: A fixed fare from €{ePrice} in a Mercedes E-Class for up to 3 passengers, €{vPrice} in the V-Class for up to 6, or €{sPrice} in the S-Class. The price includes fuel, all tolls, the Austrian and Czech vignettes and driver time — it is per car, not per person.

faqs.q: Can you pick me up at Graz Airport and drive me straight to Prague?
faqs.a: Yes. Send us your flight number when you book. Your chauffeur tracks the landing, waits inside Arrivals at Graz Airport (GRZ) with your name, and drives you directly to your Prague address. Up to 60 minutes of waiting at the airport is free.

faqs.q: Is a private transfer better than the train from Graz to Prague?
faqs.a: Most rail connections from Graz to Prague change in Vienna and take noticeably longer than the drive, before you add the trip to the station and a taxi at the Prague end. A private car is door to door and costs the same for one passenger or three. For a solo traveller with light luggage, the train is the cheaper option.

faqs.q: Can we stop on the way from Graz to Prague?
faqs.a: Yes. Linz, Český Krumlov and České Budějovice are the most popular stops; Vienna is possible as a longer detour. Tell us at booking and we include the stop in a fixed quote. A short coffee or rest break is always included at no extra cost.

faqs.q: Do I need my passport between Austria and the Czech Republic?
faqs.a: Both countries are in the Schengen Area, so there is no routine border control at Wullowitz–Dolní Dvořiště. Carry your passport or EU ID card anyway — spot checks happen, and non-EU travellers must have their documents with them.

relatedRoutesIntro: Graz is often the southern end of a trip through Austria and Central Europe. Travellers coming from Vienna, Linz, Salzburg or Bratislava book the same way — one car, one fixed fare, drop-off at the door in Prague.
